newsitem.title: GERMANY: German cocoa bean sales slow as prices edge higher.
newsitem.headline: German cocoa bean sales slow as prices edge higher.

text.p: Slightly higher cocoa futures prices deterred German cocoa bean buyers, who had already been passive for weeks, traders said on Thursday.
Traders hoped high capacity utilisation at butter and liquid producers, which pointed to good finished product sales, would work its way back into the bean market at some stage.
"Processors are fulfilling old contracts but they have not had enough new orders to justify bean purchases," one said.
"Dec futures around 980 stg/tonne are too high in any case, with consumers signalling they might buy at 20 stg below that level," he added.
Others said if there was a buying spree in the autumn, it could cause problems with immediate availability because a lot of cocoa was in the hands of one large trader.
London Dec futures were up two at 981 stg at 1400 GMT.
Local bean prices were 2.27-2.31 marks/kg for 1996 and 2.33 marks for first quarter 1997 compared with 2.22 marks quoted last week for 1996 and 2.27 marks for first quarter 1997.
The 1996 cocoa butter ratio rose one point to 2.84 and the first quarter 1997 ratio was also up one at 2.74, reflecting increased ordering from processors.
Implied cocoa butter prices liquid ex-works were 6.50-6.56 marks for the fourth quarter and 6.40 marks for Jan-March 1997, basis today's sterling rate versus the mark.
